chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the obligatory Dhihar, and he said: 'That which the man intends for Dhihar with his own self.'

key_terms.الظِّهَار: Dhihar, a form of divorce where a husband declares his wife to him as his mother's back
key_terms.بِعَيْنِهِ: With his own self / specifically himself

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Dhihar to be considered valid and obligatory in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise intent required for *Dhihar* to take effect, specifying that the husband must intend the comparison with his own physical self ('bi-'aynihi'). This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on specific verbal formulation and intent (*niyyah*) in determining the binding nature of this pre-Islamic divorce practice, distinguishing it from general comparisons.
